R004.text: Ambient n is the n-coordinate real inner product space, hence a finite-dimensional real normed vector space: its n coordinate vectors span and are independent, also for the empty coordinate family at n=0. Apply M008 to E⊆univ, M009 to this whole space, and M011 with scalar field ℝ and natural index n. This gives dimH E≤dimH(univ:Ambient n)=finrank(ℝ,Ambient n)=n. Nonnegativity is part of the [0,∞] codomain of dimH. M010 applied to E in the same space gives dimH E≠∞. No compactness or nonemptiness is used.

R005.text: In the one-dimensional real normed space ℝ, 0≠1 and 0≤1. M012 gives dimH(segment(ℝ,0,1))=1; M013 gives segment(ℝ,0,1)=[0,1]=I. Substitution proves dimH I=1.

R101.text: Fix arbitrary X,A,s, and assume L1: s>0. For an empty cover member, ediam ∅=0 and 0^s=0, so its guarded cost in Content is zero, exactly the raw diameter-power cost. For a nonempty member the supremum over its nonemptiness witnesses is that same power. Thus C_s is the stated raw countable-cover infimum. If 0<δ₁≤δ₂, each δ₁-cover is a δ₂-cover; taking infima gives C_s(δ₂,A)≤C_s(δ₁,A). Apply M001 at X,A,s. Its positive extended-scale supremum equals the positive finite real-scale supremum: every finite positive real scale is an allowed extended scale, while any h∈(0,∞] admits a finite real δ>0 with ofReal δ≤h (take δ=h.toReal/2 when h<∞, and δ=1 when h=∞). Scale antitonicity then bounds the content at h by the one at δ. This proves the normalization and supremum statements F001. The countable covers here are exactly those in problem.md; finite covers can be padded by empty sets.

Fix arbitrary real r,ε, and assume L2: H^s(A)=0, r>0 and ε>0. F001 and nonnegativity give C_s(r/2,A)=0. The defining infimum then has a cover with cost <ofReal(ε/4): if no admissible cover had cost below that positive number, the infimum would be at least that number. In particular admissible covers exist; otherwise the infimum is ∞. This proves F002.

Choose U from F002, and define d_i=(ediam U_i).toReal and e_i=ε·2^(−i−3). Since ediam U_i≤ofReal(r/2)<∞, we have 0≤d_i≤r/2<r and ediam U_i=ofReal d_i. Therefore the original cost is Σ_i ofReal(d_i^s)<ofReal(ε/4). Each e_i is positive and Σ_i e_i=ε/4: the first m terms sum to (ε/4)(1−2^(−m)), tending to ε/4. These finite partial sums also establish the corresponding extended-nonnegative sum identity.

Use M020 with exponent s≥0. For each natural index i, continuity of x↦x^s at d_i and the strict gap d_i<r from F003 permit a positive η_i smaller than r−d_i and small enough that |(d_i+η_i)^s−d_i^s|<e_i. Indeed the continuity neighborhood for error e_i>0 contains an interval about d_i, and one can take half the minimum of its positive radius and r−d_i. Then d_i+η_i is in (d_i,r) and its s-power is <d_i^s+e_i. Countable choice of these individual values yields the sequence-existence statement F004; no covering sets are enlarged.

Choose a from F004. By F003 and F004, 0<a_i≤r and ediam U_i=ofReal d_i≤ofReal a_i. Comparing nonnegative finite partial sums and then their suprema gives Σ_i ofReal(a_i^s)≤Σ_i ofReal(d_i^s)+Σ_i ofReal(e_i)<ofReal(ε/2)<ofReal ε. Addition of these nonnegative sums is justified by the finite partial-sum identity and taking increasing suprema; all right-hand totals here are finite. This proves the required cover and positive budgets for every r,ε under L2. Discharge L2 into the stated implication, and discharge L1 into the positive-exponent universal statement. Together with F001 this proves all the claimed cover-content and positive-budget statements. Empty cover members received positive numerical budgets in the same way; the proof also works in singleton and zero-dimensional spaces.

R102.text: Fix arbitrary X,A,s,δ and assume L1: s>0 and δ>0. Fix an arbitrary sequence V and assume L2: V covers A×I and ediam V_i≤ofReal δ for every i. Define ρ_i=(ediam V_i).toReal, Aproj_i=π_X(V_i), Bproj_i=π_ℝ(V_i). All ρ_i lie in [0,δ], and ediam V_i=ofReal ρ_i. The two coordinate projections are 1-Lipschitz, since each coordinate distance is bounded by their maximum, the source distance. Applying M021 to each projection therefore gives ediam Aproj_i≤ofReal ρ_i and ediam Bproj_i≤ofReal ρ_i. For empty V_i both projections and their diameters are empty and zero. This proves F001.

Each Bproj_i is bounded in ℝ. If it is empty this is immediate. Otherwise, for any t_i∈Bproj_i, every t∈Bproj_i satisfies |t−t_i|≤ρ_i by F001 and the defining diameter bound. Thus Bproj_i⊆[t_i−ρ_i,t_i+ρ_i], a bounded interval. This proves the boundedness statement F002 without choosing any measurable projection or any uniform center.

Define J_i=[inf Bproj_i,sup Bproj_i] for nonempty V_i and J_i=∅ for empty V_i. For a nonempty index, M018 and F002 give Bproj_i⊆J_i, M017 gives ediam Bproj_i=ofReal(sup Bproj_i−inf Bproj_i), and M019 gives volume(J_i)=that same quantity≤ofReal ρ_i by F001. For empty indices inclusion and the zero volume bound are immediate. Every J_i is closed (or empty), hence Borel measurable; so is J_i∩I because I is closed. M019 at 0,1 also gives volume(I)=ofReal(1−0)=1. These are F003.

Put c=C_s(δ,A) and W(t)_i=Aproj_i if t∈J_i, otherwise ∅. For each t∈I these sets cover A: for any x∈A, the cover V contains (x,t) in some V_i, hence x∈Aproj_i and t∈Bproj_i⊆J_i by F003. Each W(t)_i has extended diameter≤ofReal δ by F001, and its s-cost is at most ofReal(ρ_i^s)1_{J_i}(t), since s>0. N101's raw infimum formula yields c≤Σ_i ofReal(ρ_i^s)1_{J_i}(t). Define h=c1_I and g_i=ofReal(ρ_i^s)1_{J_i∩I}. On I the preceding inequality gives h≤Σ_i g_i; outside I both sides are zero. All g_i and h are Borel measurable: they take fixed constants on measurable sets and zero elsewhere, also when c=∞. This proves F004; we never require c to be finite.

Integrate the pointwise inequality of F004 with respect to volume on ℝ by M016. Apply M014 to the natural-indexed measurable family g, and M015 to h=c1_I and to each g_i. Using F003 and measure monotonicity gives
c=c·volume(I)=∫⁻h≤∫⁻Σ_i g_i=Σ_i∫⁻g_i
 =Σ_i ofReal(ρ_i^s) volume(J_i∩I)
 ≤Σ_i ofReal(ρ_i^s) volume(J_i)
 ≤Σ_i ofReal(ρ_i^s) ofReal ρ_i
 =Σ_i ofReal(ρ_i^(s+1))=Σ_i(ediam V_i)^(s+1).
For ρ_i>0 the last power identity is ρ_i^s·ρ_i=ρ_i^(s+1); for ρ_i=0 both s and s+1 are positive so both sides are zero. Empty indices also contribute zero. Measure monotonicity needs no additional measurability condition. Nonnegative sums are compared by finite partial sums and their suprema. These operations hold in [0,∞], with 0·∞=0 as usual; c·1=c even for c=∞. Since V was arbitrary, discharge L2 and universally quantify V. This is F005.

Take the infimum of the cover costs in F005. N101 applies to exponent s+1>0 and gives C_s(δ,A)≤C_{s+1}(δ,A×I). This infimum argument is valid even if no δ-cover exists, in which case its right-hand infimum is ∞. The argument holds for every real δ>0. Take the supremum over these scales, and use N101 for both spaces and positive exponents s and s+1, to obtain H^s(A)≤H^{s+1}(A×I). Discharge L1 and universally quantify X,A,s,δ. This proves the slicing inequality with constant one, for arbitrary subsets and without compactness.

R103.text: Fix X,A,q, and assume L1: q>0 and H^q(A)=0. Fix arbitrary real δ,ε and assume L2: δ>0 and ε>0. Define r=min(1,δ)>0. N101, instantiated with s=q and this r,ε, gives existence of a pair consisting of a cover U of A and budgets a_i with 0<a_i≤r, ediam U_i≤ofReal a_i and Σ_i ofReal(a_i^q)<ofReal ε. Record this as F001 before choosing the pair.

Choose the pair (U,a) from F001. Define N_i=ceil(1/a_i). Since 0<a_i≤r≤1, N_i≥1, 1/N_i≤a_i and N_i≤1/a_i+1≤2/a_i. Partition I by the N_i closed intervals Jpart_(i,j)=[j/N_i,(j+1)/N_i] for 0≤j<N_i. The products Ppart_(i,j)=U_i×Jpart_(i,j) cover A×I. Distances within each product are bounded by max(a_i,1/N_i)≤a_i, so its extended diameter is ≤ofReal a_i≤ofReal δ. Their index set {(i,j): i∈ℕ,0≤j<N_i} injects into ℕ×ℕ, which is enumerated by successive finite diagonals. Thus the products can be reindexed as a natural sequence, with empty padding if necessary. Reindexing preserves the sum of nonnegative costs: both are suprema of the same finite subfamily sums. Their total (q+1)-cost satisfies
Σ_i Σ_{j<N_i}(ediam Ppart_(i,j))^(q+1)
 ≤Σ_i ofReal(N_i a_i^(q+1))
 ≤Σ_i ofReal((2/a_i)a_i^(q+1))
 =2Σ_i ofReal(a_i^q)<ofReal(2ε).
All divisions are by positive a_i; real powers give a_i^(q+1)/a_i=a_i^q. This proves the countable-cover existence and cost bound F002, with absolute constant 2.

N101 identifies C_{q+1}(δ,A×I) with the cover-cost infimum. By F002 it is ≤ofReal(2ε) for every ε>0 at each fixed δ>0, so it is zero: any positive finite lower bound is contradicted by taking a smaller ε, and even one such finite bound excludes ∞. Discharge L2 to obtain the asserted existence for every δ,ε>0 and zero content for every δ>0. N101's finite-positive-scale supremum then yields H^{q+1}(A×I)=0. Discharge L1 and universally quantify X,A,q. This proves both claimed clauses, including the scale/tolerance statement and its constant.

R104.text: Fix X,A and assume L1: A is nonempty. This says precisely that there exists a point x₀∈A, the existence recorded as F001.

Choose x₀∈A from F001 and define f:ℝ→MaxProd X by f(t)=(x₀,t). For all real t,u, d_max(f(t),f(u))=max(d_X(x₀,x₀),|t−u|)=max(0,|t−u|)=|t−u|. Thus f is both 1-Lipschitz and 1-antilipschitz. Also f '' I⊆A×I, because x₀∈A. Record these facts as F002.

Apply M006 and M007 to f and I using F002; their two opposite image inequalities give dimH(f '' I)=dimH I. N005 says dimH I=1. Apply M008 in MaxProd X to the inclusion in F002, obtaining 1=dimH(f '' I)≤dimH(A×I). Discharge L1 and quantify X,A. This proves the claimed lower bound; the chosen point's identity is absent from the conclusion.

R105.text: Fix X,A and assume L1: A is nonempty and dimH A≠∞. Define D0=(dimH A).toReal and G=A×I. Since dimH A is finite and nonnegative, D0≥0 and ofReal D0=dimH A. This establishes F001 and legitimately permits approximation by real exponents.

Fix an arbitrary real q and assume L2: q>D0. Then q>0 by F001. Instantiate M003 with subset A and nonnegative exponent q: ofReal q>dimH A, so H^q(A)=0. N103 with X,A,q yields H^{q+1}(G)=0. Record this exact measure conclusion as F002.

Apply M004 in MaxProd X to G and exponent q+1>0, using F002's zero measure (zero≠∞). It gives dimH G≤ofReal(q+1). Since q was arbitrary, discharge L2 into the complete universally quantified assertion F003.

Take q0=D0+1 in F003; the resulting finite upper bound proves dimH G≠∞. Define T0=(dimH G).toReal, so T0≥0 and ofReal T0=dimH G. To prove the sharp upper bound, assume L3: T0>D0+1, and define qmid=D0+(T0−D0−1)/2. Then qmid>D0 and qmid+1<T0. F003 at qmid gives T0≤qmid+1, a contradiction. Discharge L3 by classical contradiction, obtaining T0≤D0+1. Independently, N104 applies to the nonempty A from F001 and gives dimH G≥1, hence T0≥1. These finite-dimension and bound facts are F004.
Fix an arbitrary real s and assume L4: 0<s<D0. By F001, ofReal s<dimH A. M002 at subset A and nonnegative exponent s gives H^s(A)=∞, the exact assertion F005.
Instantiate N102 with X,A,s. Since s>0, F005 and its measure inequality give ∞=H^s(A)≤H^{s+1}(A×I)=H^{s+1}(G), so H^{s+1}(G)=∞. This is F006.
Apply M005 in MaxProd X at subset G and exponent s+1, using F006. It gives ofReal(s+1)≤dimH G, hence s+1≤T0 by F004. Discharge L4 and quantify the arbitrary s to obtain F007.

By D0≥0 from F001, the cases D0=0 and D0>0 are exhaustive. In the first branch assume L5: D0=0. F004 gives T0≥1=D0+1; close this branch and discharge L5. In the second branch assume L6: D0>0. To prove T0≥D0+1 assume L7: T0<D0+1 and define smid=(max(0,T0−1)+D0)/2. Both 0 and T0−1 are <D0, so max(0,T0−1)<smid<D0. In particular smid>0 and T0<smid+1, whereas F007 gives smid+1≤T0. This is a contradiction; discharge L7, obtaining T0≥D0+1 in this branch, and discharge L6. Case elimination therefore gives T0≥D0+1 universally. With F004's opposite bound, T0=D0+1. Since ofReal D0=dimH A and ofReal T0=dimH G, this is dimH(A×I)=dimH A+1 in [0,∞]. The finiteness clause is F004. Discharge L1 and quantify X,A; this proves the claimed dimension equality and finiteness, including the case D0=0.

R106.text:
The map appendCoord(n) places the n coordinates of its first component before its real second component. Its inverse reads off these first n coordinates and the last coordinate. These coordinate operations are inverse in both orders, so the map is bijective. Fix arbitrary source points p,p′ and put a=‖p.1−p′.1‖₂≥0, b=|p.2−p′.2|≥0. Splitting the finite sum of squares into the first n terms and the last term gives
 d₂(appendCoord(n)p,appendCoord(n)p′)^2
   =Σ_{i<n}|p.1_i−p′.1_i|²+|p.2−p′.2|²=a²+b².
Since max(a,b)²≤a²+b²≤2max(a,b)², taking nonnegative square roots gives
 d_max(p,p′)≤d₂(appendCoord(n)p,appendCoord(n)p′)≤√2·d_max(p,p′).
The maximum is exactly the source distance. Quantifying p,p′, these inequalities establish √2-Lipschitz and 1-antilipschitz bounds. When n=0, the coordinate sum is empty and zero, the first component is the unique vector of Ambient 0, and the same inverse and estimates still apply. Record the full construction and bounds as F001.

Fix an arbitrary subset S⊆MaxProd(Ambient n). Apply M006 with map appendCoord(n) and K=√2≥0, using F001, to obtain dimH(appendCoord(n) '' S)≤dimH S. Apply M007 with the same map and L=1, again using F001, to obtain the reverse inequality. Antisymmetry gives equality for every S. Together with F001's bijectivity and the two explicit distance bounds, this proves the claimed metric bridge and dimension preservation. Both constants are absolute; no norm-invariance assertion is assumed.

R107.text: Return to the original natural n and E⊆Ambient n. H001 gives that E is nonempty. N004 gives dimH E≤n and dimH E≠∞, including n=0. Instantiate N105 with X=Ambient n and A=E. Its nonemptiness and finite-dimension conditions are exactly these two available facts. It yields dimH(E×I)=dimH E+1 in MaxProd(Ambient n), and finiteness of that product dimension. Now apply N106 to the subset E×I. Under the fixed coordinate identification, appendCoord(n) '' (E×I) is precisely the original E×[0,1] in Euclidean ℝ^(n+1): its first n coordinates belong to E and its last coordinate belongs to [0,1], and conversely every such vector has this preimage. N106 transfers the maximum-metric dimension to this Euclidean image. Therefore dimH(E×[0,1])=dimH E+1 with the stipulated Euclidean metric. Both sides are finite by N004 and N105, so their [0,∞] equality is the equality of finite real dimensions as well. This proves P. The original compactness hypothesis remains retained but is unused in this strengthened basis route.

156:    repair. Normal final machine Audit B inherits the frozen semantic review;

159:    `nl02lean/scripts/source_preparation.py` for bounded shared extraction,

162:    statement or new theorem returns to the affected NL0/Audit A boundary.

167: ## Mathematical invariants

191:   closure and trust, without a Mathlib-to-NL0 use ledger.

1: # Shared-lemma extraction as a local NL0 revision
2: 
3: ## Scope and position
4: 
5: Apply this procedure at the start of **NL0-to-Lean translation**, before final
6: interface/planning freeze or worker-packet generation. It is not an extra
7: requirement for a task that requests NL0 alone. The input is an existing,
8: versioned NL0, not an invitation to reconstruct its proof.
9: 
10: The operation is proof factoring: move an already supplied local derivation
11: into one shared N/R pair and replace its occurrences by explicit applications.
12: Do not rewrite the whole NL0, regenerate its prose, reprove unchanged results,
13: or seek a stronger/general theorem for speculative future reuse. Reading the
14: existing graph to locate candidates is not a new proof-construction task.
15: If an existing N already exports the needed fact, reuse that node directly.
16: 
17: Use [the revision record](../templates/source-refactoring.md). Preserve the
18: original package and audit as immutable evidence. Write a revised package in
19: a new directory; retain existing IDs and keep the revision identity in the
20: sidecar record. Generated Markdown/diagrams are views, never patch authorities.
21: 
22: ## 1. Locate and qualify candidates without reconstructing NL0
23: 
24: Start with existing node statements, direct inputs, definitions and any
25: available index. Locate repeated subarguments using their mathematical role,
26: objects, formulas or operation names; then inspect the actual candidate spans
27: and the local context they need. Do not commission a new proof or a full prose
28: summary for every node as a discovery method. Text similarity is only a lead.
29: 
30: For each proposed lemma record:
31: 
32: - The complete mathematical statement, all parameters/conditions and proposed
33:   direct input IDs, together with exact old graph pointers or paragraph spans.
34: - The existing derivation to reuse and every occurrence that will consume it.
35:   The derivation must actually supply the proposed statement; a summary label
36:   or a theorem believed true from memory is insufficient.
37: - Identify the baseline revision/old paragraph IDs separately from the current
38:   new producer. A new N's origin label must state the historical/current
39:   distinction; a bare old R number is ambiguous after consumer editing.
40: - The expected avoided repeated work. An occurrence count is not measured
41:   formalization cost and does not by itself establish a speed benefit.
42: - The scope at each occurrence, including bound variables, temporary
43:   assumptions, definition guards and local facts established before the span.
44: 
45: Prefer a statement already justified at the cuts. Do not generalize its domain,
46: change representations, weaken conditions or introduce new mathematics merely
47: to make more occurrences match. If the proposed derivation needs an earlier
48: local calculation, include that calculation with its justified inputs. Never
49: declare an unexported local fact to be an available graph input.
50: 
51: Temporary assumptions stay closed in an implication or other complete
52: proposition; they cannot become H roots. An extraction that moves a witness,
53: choice, definition or binder across a scope boundary needs an explicit account
54: of the values and properties used afterwards. If that account cannot be made
55: locally and clearly, leave the original argument in place.
56: 
57: ## 2. Write the patch boundary before editing
58: 
59: Prepare an edit allowlist for one candidate or one coherent batch:
60: 
61: | Part | Allowed edit |
62: | --- | --- |
63: | New shared theorem | One fresh N and its R producer, with a complete statement and derivation from existing permitted inputs. |
64: | Actual consumers | Replace only the located repeated proof spans by a complete application; adjust direct inputs, citations and application accounting accordingly. |
65: | Necessary local bookkeeping | Update the directly affected binder/reference accounting and generated views. Record every such edit explicitly. |
66: | Everything else | Preserve the existing record content; do not reorder or renumber it as a cleanup. |
67: 
68: Keep the entire frozen specification unchanged: target P, original H, parameter
69: domains, global definitions/notation, logic, pins and E/M source inventories and
70: statements. Preserve all existing N/P statements and every unmodified argument
71: span. New sources, changed hypotheses, new global definitions, removed existing
72: nodes, or a changed old output are outside this fast factoring operation.
73: 
74: Copy an existing derivation rather than writing a new proof route. The new
75: producer may use only its declared inputs, global definitions and legitimate
76: local derivations. It cannot depend on a consumer output or its descendants.
77: Do not split each consumer into additional source nodes around the shared fact.
78: 
79: Each consumer application must state the parameter substitution, which inputs
80: or local proved facts discharge each condition, and the exact conclusion used.
81: Remove a former direct input only if the remaining argument no longer uses it;
82: retain it when it still has a direct role. A shared theorem is never ambient.
83: 
84: If an edit escapes the allowlist, return that candidate to the shortlist or
85: leave it unextracted. A source defect goes through the existing gap procedure;
86: do not turn a reuse optimization into a repair or a new research route.
87: 
88: ## 3. Check structural preservation globally, reasoning locally
89: 
90: Compare canonical JSON records by stable IDs, not only rendered text or changed
91: line numbers. Record before/after hashes and the actual changed fields/spans.
92: Reject any unexplained diff. Check these global mechanical invariants:
93: 
94: - The frozen specification and protected records are unchanged.
95: - All IDs/references resolve; definitions and guards remain available; there
96:   is no cycle or unsupported initial node; every N/P still has one producer.
97: - Every retained node remains in P's dependency closure. Reject the candidate
98:   if it would require deleting or reorganizing unrelated nodes to restore this.
99: - All consumers declare their actual inputs and remain self-contained. Only
100:   the explicit allowlisted nodes/fields have changed.
101: 
102: Run the existing `../scripts/nl0.py check` on the revised graph and specification.
103: Rechecking graph metadata across the package is allowed and inexpensive relative
104: to rereading every mathematical proof. It does not require a new LLM proof of
105: every node, and it does not establish the semantics of a substitution.
106: 
107: Distinguish **review impact** from **dependency status**. The new producer and
108: edited application boundaries need new mathematical review. An unchanged
109: downstream proof whose input statements and conventions are unchanged need not
110: be reconstructed merely because its ancestors have a new producer. Its final
111: acceptance nevertheless depends on the replacement producer being accepted.
112: Until that happens, affected descendants are pending, not newly accepted.
113: 
114: ## 4. Incremental Audit A: review the new proof and the substitution cuts
115: 
116: This is an incremental review procedure under Audit A's mathematical
117: obligations, not permission to weaken source verification or invent a fresh
118: packet replay. The version-bound receipt limitation below is part of the rule.
119: 
120: First inspect the baseline audit and its evidence bindings. Reuse a judgment
121: only for the exact previously reviewed content, context and evidence. Carry
122: FAIL, UNVERIFIED, inaccessible sources and disclosure limits forward. A source
123: file hash proves byte identity, not that an auditor ever inspected the theorem.
124: An unaudited baseline cannot acquire whole-proof acceptance through extraction.
125: 
126: Review the **new N/R in full**: complete statement, exact inputs, argument,
127: dependency accounting, scopes, guards and E/M applications, and the normal
128: fresh packet-only replay requirement. The extracted proof may be copied, but
129: its new closed interface and context must actually be checked.
130: 
131: For **each changed consumer**, review a substitution cut rather than rewriting
132: or replaying its entire old proof by default:
133: 
134: 1. Compare the old derived conclusion at the cut with the instantiated shared
135:    result, including all conditions, quantifiers and semantic conventions.
136: 2. Check that every condition of the shared theorem follows from that consumer's
137:    declared inputs or explicit in-scope local derivations, without extra facts.
138: 3. Check the interface to the untouched continuation: every subsequently used
139:    proposition, object, value and scope remains available with the same meaning.
140:    Equal output text alone cannot establish preservation of a selected witness.
141: 4. Verify the changed direct-input/citation/application accounting. Reuse source
142:    identity evidence only when unchanged; check every new source application.
143: 5. Bind the untouched remainder to its old reviewed bytes and old review
144:    evidence. Record exactly which old checks are inherited and which new checks
145:    cover the patch. Do not relabel this comparison as a new fresh whole-R replay.
146: 
147: If those boundaries do not justify inheritance, mark that candidate
148: `DEFERRED_NOT_LOCAL` and keep the baseline argument. Do not automatically expand
149: to a full-case audit. A separately requested broader review may inspect the
150: specific unresolved node, but is not part of this fast extraction.
151: 
152: Unchanged target/source/definition reviews and proof regions need no new
153: mathematical re-review when their audited content, applicable context and
154: evidence are unchanged. Do not reopen source searches solely because a global
155: graph hash changed. Changes or failures in their evidence invalidate reuse.
156: 
157: The result is a chain: baseline audit + exact revision + actual new reviews.
158: It is not a copied PASS with an updated graph hash. Record actual reviewer
159: exposure; old-review access is appropriate for delta review and cannot be called
160: an independent fresh packet-only review. This procedure authorizes no additional
161: agent or external-service dispatch.
162: 
163: ## 5. Seal or leave the candidate unextracted
164: 
165: Seal only after the allowlist/diff and graph checks pass and the scoped
166: mathematical review is complete. Keep original and revised manifests, patch,
167: location map, old/new evidence, pending findings and measured preparation cost.
168: Stage all candidate edits transactionally; a failed candidate must not replace
169: the accepted baseline. Do not launch formalization workers for an unaccepted
170: source revision or reuse task packets bound to the old graph.
171: 
172: Then finalize and freeze typed interfaces, shared Lean ports and local plans;
173: only afterwards generate worker packets. Shared Lean interface discovery may
174: use this preparation pass, but must not silently mutate the sealed NL0 later.
175: No extraction is a valid outcome; do not manufacture shared lemmas to satisfy
176: the workflow. The work is bounded by the chosen proof regions and patch size,
177: not a universal minute count. Longer time alone is not a mathematical gap.
178: 
179: ## Executable acceptance and review responsibilities
180: 
181: The unchanged parent checker still binds ordinary format-4 audit to the complete
182: graph. `scripts/source_preparation.py` adds a separate incremental record;
183: it never copies old PASS fields into a forged fresh whole-graph audit.
184: Audit B and `workflow.py` both revalidate that record and all underlying evidence.
185: See [commands and the patch contract](integrated-workflow.md).
186: 
187: The initial executable scope is current-v2 source and nonoverlapping consumer
188: paragraph substitutions. Old proposition records/specification, unlisted R
189: records, untouched paragraphs and local fact/assumption lifetimes are protected.
190: Consumer source-application changes can remove obsolete uses, not introduce new
191: external uses. A broader refactor is deferred rather than widening this operation.
192: Multiple proposed edits to one consumer must first be merged into one coherent
193: candidate or left unextracted. Legacy test copies remain development evidence.
194: 
195: Separate three responsibilities:
196: 
197: - A producer reviewer sees only the complete new per-R packet and audits its
198:   conditional mathematics under ordinary Audit A, including actual fresh replay.
199:   Do not ask that packet to establish whole-graph acceptance or old-copy provenance.
200: - A substitution reviewer sees paired before/after consumers, the proposed shared
201:   statement, original derivations and explicit cut contract. `old_derivation`
202:   names THIS consumer's replaced proof; `producer_source_derivation` names the
203:   one original proof used to export the shared lemma. Its supplier may be a
204:   different consumer with a different final goal. Compare the common intermediate
205:   conclusion, not equality of those final goals. Check existing-proof
206:   factoring, each condition, exact supplied conclusion, continuation and accounting.
207:   This is delta review with baseline access, not fresh whole-consumer replay.
208: - Python checks canonical fanout, edit scope, graph validity, immutable evidence,
209:   the exact coverage partition and inherited acceptance/qualifications. It does
210:   not judge natural-language mathematics or authenticate a dishonest reviewer.
211: 
212: Internal N applications are direct inputs, paragraph citations and explicit prose;
213: the parent's `applications` source records remain E/M-only. Do not invent an N
214: source-application record to satisfy a reviewer. A prose citation without a real
215: substitution is not successful factoring. Derivation labels and fanout guesses
216: from a model are leads, not canonical graph facts.
217: 
218: Each cut review binds the exact supplied packet hash. Retain the binding from
219: the generated template and verify it during acceptance. Reusing an actual old
220: review after a record-only change requires identical canonical mathematics and
221: byte-identical actual reviewed packets; preserve its verdicts, notes, evidence
222: and original cost, and disclose that no new mathematical review occurred.
223: 
224: `INCREMENTAL-AUDIT-A-PASSED` requires a passing current baseline plus all actual
225: new producer/cut reviews. Missing/failed baseline checks remain inherited and
226: yield development-only local review. Every later consumer acceptance still
227: depends on the new producer; unchanged input statements and context permit
228: inheriting the old conditional argument without rereading it mathematically.
229: No fixed completion-time threshold makes a candidate worthwhile or incorrect.

1: # Audit A: mathematical review in Yui
2: 
3: <!-- yui-nl0-acceptance:begin -->
4: ## Shared mathematical acceptance requirements
5: 
6: Contract version: `yui-nl0-audit-a-2`.
7: 
8: The author and independent auditor use this same mathematical standard. NL0
9: reviews a complete natural-language proof and necessary mathematical detail.
10: Specific Lean declarations, signatures, representations and proof tactics are
11: implementation work for nl02lean, not prerequisites for ordinary NL0 review.
12: The following grouped criteria replace V1's ten separate per-R report rows.
13: 
14: | ID | Review group | Author evidence group | Requirement |
15: | --- | --- | --- | --- |
16: | `target` | package | original_context_note | Preserve the complete original theorem, every original H, quantifier, domain, normalization, parameter range, constant dependency and supplied active proof route. In explicit 2basis mode, the original task remains target/H authority and the basis proof is the authorized active route; review both, including replacements and new derivations. A parameter or definition cannot hide a hypothesis or desired conclusion. |
17: | `definitions` | package | declaration_check | Define mathematical objects and notation sufficiently for their actual uses. Check types, dependencies, construction guards and legitimate local introductions. A definition grants no unproved property. |
18: | `sources` | package | original_context_note | Check complete E statements, primary-source identity, context and conditions under the source policy. An explicitly selected native M retains its bound signature checks; authors need not introduce M nodes for ordinary mathematical background. Unavailable originals remain disclosed UNVERIFIED source assumptions. |
19: | `structure` | package | original_context_note | Verify the actual AND dependency graph, unique producers, absence of cycles and faithful exported statements. Retain every original H and disclose unused H. Internal results are proved, never new roots. |
20: | `statement_closure` | closure | output_notes | Inputs and output state the mathematical content, objects, domains, quantifiers and conditions their consumers need. Check actual object occurrences and definitions. No missing identification can be supplied by an absent producer proof or a paper equation number. |
21: | `dependency_closure` | closure | dependency_and_local_assumption_check | Check direct input use, earlier local facts, witness existence and proper discharge of assumptions. No circular dependency, future fact or escaped local object is allowed. Mathematically checked routine background may supplement the packet without prior native lookup. |
22: | `argument` | inference | dependency_and_local_assumption_check | Verify the complete implication and every output clause at ordinary rigorous mathematical granularity, including material limiting operations, domains and regularity. Compress correct routine reasoning; locate a real gap rather than requiring a transcript of elementary steps. |
23: | `applicability` | inference | source_application_check | Check actual instantiations and all material premises of invoked E/M or routine background facts, with grounds in inputs or earlier local derivations. Required bridges are proved. A familiar theorem name or a proposed Lean tactic supplies no mathematical justification. |
24: 
25: ### Scope and mathematical boundary
26: 
27: Global review owns target/H fidelity, definitions, source statements and graph
28: consistency. Each local reviewer owns the conditional implication at its R
29: node. Conditional packet replay has a different input boundary: these statements are conditional premises.
30: The local reviewer does not re-prove an input N or re-audit its source paper;
31: the graph and that producer's review establish those separate obligations.
32: Conversely, an input N exports only its full statement, not unexported facts
33: from the producer's body. The fifth local criterion, packet_replay, assesses
34: sufficiency under this exact boundary. The controller records execution
35: identity and exposure independently of the mathematical judgment.
36: 
37: Review correctness rather than the number of displayed lines. Ordinary valid
38: textbook compression is allowed. Material missing hypotheses, witnesses,
39: constructions, scope discharges or core arguments are not implementation gaps.
40: Return them for located author repair and fresh review. No theorem needs to be re-proved
41: when its legitimate mathematical source and actual application suffice.
42: 
43: The domain-neutral elementary-language-4 profile retains equality, supplied
44: definitions, finite arithmetic/order reasoning and finite sums. It is syntax
45: and elementary calculation policy, not a subject vocabulary or theorem list.
46: Objects from any field use problem parameters, D definitions or scoped locals.
47: Neither an author-written calculation list nor a familiar symbol adds a theorem.
48: 
49: ### Mathematical background: mathematical-background-v2-1
50: 
51: A reviewer may positively assess a routine, local mathematical fact without
52: first finding its Mathlib declaration. Record its precise mathematical
53: statement, actual argument location, available condition grounds and a short
54: mathematical justification in a background note. Use kind mathematical for an
55: ordinary background result and elementary for a useful elementary completion.
56: This is an actual mathematical judgment, not a future TODO or a claim of
57: native verification. Do not record every algebraic operation.
58: 
59: Eligibility requires a correct standard local step with all premises already
60: available, no new H and no substantial new core proof or changed route.
61: Important external tools remain explicit E inputs; a missing project result
62: or uncertain source cannot be waived as background. If an explicitly supplied
63: native mathlib note is retained, its full bound evidence is still validated.
64: No field-specific whitelist determines eligibility.
65: 
66: The accepted authority is immutable author NL0 plus its hash-bound mathematical
67: review supplement. It is a natural-language audit under the mathematical-background policy, not a
68: detailed-NL0 format-3 native-background receipt. At nl02lean, workers must discharge all necessary
69: facts by actual Lean proofs or checked library use; a note never becomes an
70: unproved H, axiom or extra external assumption. The exact implementation may
71: differ while preserving the mathematical meaning.
72: 
73: ### Actual review and result qualification
74: 
75: Independent reviewers assess the actual content; schema validation does not
76: prove mathematics. An unexamined item remains unread/read. A mathematical
77: uncertainty is assessed UNVERIFIED, not PASS. Missing or conflicting assessments
78: block acceptance. Ordinary source-access deferral follows the conditional-source
79: policy and must appear in final warnings; it cannot yield unqualified PASS.
80: 
81: Use short located reasons for straightforward PASS items and enough detail to
82: make a defect or uncertainty actionable. Avoid duplicate explanations across
83: criteria. A concise report still covers every required mathematical check.
84: Do not read author self-check notes, old verdicts, other R proof bodies, other
85: case results or personal proof skills to manufacture independent approval.
86: <!-- yui-nl0-acceptance:end -->
87: 
88: ## Execution protocol
89: 
90: 1. Freeze the original problem, spec and NL0. A separate fresh global reviewer
91:    reads the exhaustive global-overview.json, relevant canonical content and
92:    source evidence. Review each D and selected E/M; the overview is data, not
93:    an assessment. Do not infer absence from a partial page.
94: 2. Complete global source/graph review before dispatching local R reviews.
95:    Independent R reviewers use the current R-node count as their default slot
96:    limit, or the user's explicit positive N cap.
97:    Each receives only its own packet and mathematical-NL0 rules. Review full arguments,
98:    actual applications and definitions; input N statements are conditional.
99: 3. Prefer one complete artifact with an explicit coverage map. Use
100:    record_review_item and read_review_progress only for useful checkpoints.
101:    record_background_note is optional; a complete artifact may include its
102:    actual notes directly. Batch reading several declared fragments is available.
103: 4. The generated tool schema defines the current submission fields and selected
104:    review IDs. Each local report has inference, packet_sha256, verdict, notes, checks,
105:    findings and optional background_notes. The checks map contains exactly
106:    statement_closure, dependency_closure, argument, applicability, packet_replay.
107:    Each row has verdict, notes and resolving packet locations. E applications
108:    additionally retain actual binding, per-hypothesis, conclusion and bridge
109:    assessments; this is mathematical applicability, not a Lean API inventory.
110: 5. Global reports have target_review, definition_reviews, source_reviews,
111:    structure_review and findings. An incremental review includes only its
112:    assigned scopes, as specified in its generated schema. Local report-level
113:    verdict and notes fields are not global summary fields. Each E adds citation_checks for
114:    literature_identity, result_location, statement_fidelity,
115:    context_completeness, version_and_eligibility. Inaccessible primary text
116:    leaves blocked checks UNVERIFIED while remaining assessment continues.
117: 6. A blocking finding needs its actual location, explanation and a short exact
118:    quotation from that location. Preserve the defect and untouched coverage.
119:    Return located mathematical repairs to the author; review changed scopes
120:    independently. Do not resample a mathematical rejection or silently erase it.
121: 7. The collector checks complete coverage, consistency, exact bytes and actual
122:    independent execution before producing the audit-format-4 receipt.
123:    Old detailed-NL0 format-3 receipts are not silently upgraded. Inherited format-4 judgments retain
124:    their original source/rule hashes, exposure and costs.
125: 
126: ## Sources, scopes and final handoff
127: 
128: Use [external theorem review](external-theorems.md) and
129: [conditional sources](conditional-sources.md) for source identity, exact
130: statements and warnings. Reuse adequate original text; several theorem uses
131: may share one staged readback. Each application still discharges its own
132: premises. No successful download or guessed Mathlib availability is approval.
133: 
134: Use [logical rules](logical-rules.md) for local scopes and
135: [background notes](background-notes.md) for the mathematical supplement.
136: The ordinary complete result remains relative to explicit E assumptions.
137: An inaccessible E original permits only a source-qualified result. Translation
138: retains this exact audit and supplement until reviewed mathematical changes
139: invalidate affected scopes. Typed interfaces, native checking, standalone
140: assembly and independent semantic Audit B are separate later gates.
141: 
142: ## Paywalled or inaccessible primary text
143: 
144: Follow [conditional sources](conditional-sources.md). Preserve the complete
145: secondary statement and actual access evidence; unavailable source checks
146: stay UNVERIFIED. Continue other work only with an explicitly qualified source
147: assumption, and report warn.json/warn.md. No unqualified full PASS is granted.

definitions.definition: H^u(B)=μH[u](B) denotes Mathlib's unnormalized Hausdorff measure, the metric measure mkMetric for the gauge r↦r^u on the Borel sigma algebra. The metric-measure construction takes countable-cover outer contents for this gauge, with the empty-set gauge cost forced to zero, and their supremum as the scale tends to zero. Its precise cover evaluation will be applied as an explicit native source, rather than assumed as an extra premise. No spherical or dimensional normalization factor is used.

definitions.type: subset of an extended metric space → [0,∞]
definitions.definition: For B in an extended metric space, equipped with its Borel measurable structure when computing H, dimH(B)=sup{d∈[0,∞): H^d(B)=∞}, the supremum taken in [0,∞] and with sup ∅=0. This is native Mathlib dimH. Positive-exponent critical-exponent directions are invoked as explicit native sources. We use no zero-exponent measure assertion.

definitions.definition: I=[0,1]={t∈ℝ:0≤t≤1}. This is unitInterval in the basis header.

For a metric space Z, MaxProd(Z)=Z×ℝ with distance d_max((x,t),(y,u))=max(d_Z(x,y),|t−u|). For B⊆Z, B×I always denotes a subset of MaxProd(Z) in intermediate lemmas. All metric spaces in integration or Hausdorff-measure statements carry their Borel sigma algebra.

appendCoord(m)(x,t) is the vector whose first m coordinates are those of x and whose last coordinate is t. In the exact basis header it is WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.lastCases t (fun j => x j)). Its target always carries the Euclidean norm; its source here carries the maximum metric. It is a total coordinate construction, including m=0. Under the problem's identification ℝ^n×ℝ=ℝ^(n+1), the Euclidean set E×[0,1] is appendCoord(n) '' (E×I).

definitions.type: measure on the Borel sets of ℝ
definitions.definition: volume is Lebesgue measure on ℝ, with its usual Borel measurable structure (and its extension as an outer measure on arbitrary sets). Thus measure monotonicity applies to all subsets; no measurability of a covering set is implicit.
For a set B⊆Z and a scalar c∈[0,∞], c1_B denotes the function equal to c on B and zero off B, that is B.indicator(fun _ => c). This is meaningful for c=∞ as well, with no subtraction of infinities.

For a measurable space Z, measure μ and f:Z→[0,∞], ∫⁻ f dμ (the lower Lebesgue integral, lintegral) is the supremum of ∫g dμ over measurable nonnegative simple functions g≤f; a simple function integral is its finite sum of values times the measures of the corresponding disjoint level sets. All integrals in the slicing proof are lower integrals; integrability is never required.

definitions.definition: LipschitzWith(K,f) means ∀x,y, edist(f x,f y)≤K·edist(x,y), where K is a finite nonnegative real embedded into [0,∞]. On metric spaces this is the usual distance inequality.

definitions.definition: AntilipschitzWith(L,f) means ∀x,y, edist(x,y)≤L·edist(f x,f y), with finite L≥0. On metric spaces this is the corresponding ordinary distance inequality.

definitions.definition: segment(k,x,y)={a•x+b•y: a,b∈k, a≥0,b≥0,a+b=1}, in a vector space over an ordered scalar field k; over ℝ this is the usual closed line segment.

finrank(k,Z) is the dimension as a natural number of a finite-dimensional k-vector space Z (and is zero by the native total convention if the vector-space rank is infinite). In this proof its arguments are finite dimensional.

definitions.definition: The notation v^u uses the standard real power; on positive real v it is exp(u log v), with 0^u=0 for u>0 and 0^0=1. For extended nonnegative bases it is the usual extension: at u>0, ∞^u=∞ and 0^u=0; at u=0 the value is 1; at u<0, 0^u=∞ and ∞^u=0. Only nonnegative real bases and positive exponents occur in the covering calculations. The native real function at negative v is defined using |v|, as in Real.rpow.

argument.text:
The map appendCoord(n) places the n coordinates of its first component before its real second component. Its inverse reads off these first n coordinates and the last coordinate. These coordinate operations are inverse in both orders, so the map is bijective. Fix arbitrary source points p,p′ and put a=‖p.1−p′.1‖₂≥0, b=|p.2−p′.2|≥0. Splitting the finite sum of squares into the first n terms and the last term gives
 d₂(appendCoord(n)p,appendCoord(n)p′)^2
   =Σ_{i<n}|p.1_i−p′.1_i|²+|p.2−p′.2|²=a²+b².
Since max(a,b)²≤a²+b²≤2max(a,b)², taking nonnegative square roots gives
 d_max(p,p′)≤d₂(appendCoord(n)p,appendCoord(n)p′)≤√2·d_max(p,p′).
The maximum is exactly the source distance. Quantifying p,p′, these inequalities establish √2-Lipschitz and 1-antilipschitz bounds. When n=0, the coordinate sum is empty and zero, the first component is the unique vector of Ambient 0, and the same inverse and estimates still apply. Record the full construction and bounds as F001.

produces.statement: appendCoord(n):MaxProd(Ambient n)→Ambient(n+1) is bijective, is √2-Lipschitz and 1-antilipschitz, and its distances satisfy d_max(p0,p1)≤d₂(appendCoord(n)p0,appendCoord(n)p1)≤√2·d_max(p0,p1) for all source points p0,p1. This holds including n=0.

argument.text: Fix an arbitrary subset S⊆MaxProd(Ambient n). Apply M006 with map appendCoord(n) and K=√2≥0, using F001, to obtain dimH(appendCoord(n) '' S)≤dimH S. Apply M007 with the same map and L=1, again using F001, to obtain the reverse inequality. Antisymmetry gives equality for every S. Together with F001's bijectivity and the two explicit distance bounds, this proves the claimed metric bridge and dimension preservation. Both constants are absolute; no norm-invariance assertion is assumed.
